assertions.description: \A, \z and \Z are valid Assertions in a u-flag pattern: new RegExp(String.raw`\A\z\Z`, 'u') compiles instead of throwing SyntaxError ("Invalid escape" in engines without the proposal).
The escapes are equally valid under the v flag (UnicodeSets mode is Unicode mode): new RegExp(String.raw`\A[\w--\d]+\z`, 'v') compiles and matches "abc".
\A matches only at input index 0 even with the m flag: /\Afoo/mu matches "foo\nbar" but not "bar\nfoo".
assertions.test: (() => { const re = new RegExp(String.raw`\Afoo`, 'mu'); return re.test('foo\nbar') && !re.test('bar\nfoo'); })()

assertions.description: Without u or v the escapes stay Annex B identity escapes for the letters A, z and Z: /\Afoo\z/ matches "Afooz" and does not match "foo".
assertions.test: (() => { const re = new RegExp(String.raw`\Afoo\z`); return re.test('Afooz') && !re.test('foo'); })()

assertions.description: The escapes are not added to ClassEscape: [\A] in a u-flag pattern is still a SyntaxError.
\A is an Assertion, which cannot take a quantifier in Unicode mode: /\A*/u is a SyntaxError.

A regex literal using the escapes parses as script source: Function('return /\\Afoo\\z/u')() returns a RegExp matching "foo". Without the feature this is an early SyntaxError that fails the whole script.
